doc.title: Karolina Strassmayer interviewed by Monk Rowe, May 25, 2023

chapter: New York and the WDR Big Band
title: Doubling on flute and clarinet and passing parts around
summary: Doubles are essential for big bands; WDR members pass doubles and solos to whoever suits them.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: I assume that gig required some doubling and were you prepared for that?

Yes. Yes I was prepared for that. In Diva also we played a lot of doubles and I played a lot of gigs in New York with various big bands. And I realized that doubling is so crucial. You just don’t get called for these kind of bands if you don’t have your flute and clarinet together. And clarinet is not my favorite instrument but on the flute I feel comfortable so that is definitely my stronger double and in the WDR Big Band even though all of us play all the doubles, each one of us has stronger doubles and things or if you feel more comfortable then we just pass those parts around and I usually end up with the flute and the piccolo parts. And Johan Horlen, who is the lead alto player in the WDR Big band, he is a very strong clarinetist so he’s happy to play the clarinet parts. So we worked it out amongst ourselves.

That reminds me of a conversation I just had with a couple of the top lead trumpet players in Los Angeles and they said that, that sometimes — well there’s a part here and you know what you’d be a lot better on it so “pass it on” they would say.

Yeah. And that’s how we do it in the WDR Big Band too. And most of the writers already know anyway who to write the piccolo part for, or the alto flute part, or the clarinet solo. They know, or they ask. Or even when there are solos, where one of us feels more comfortable in this stylistic environment or not so comfortable in that, then we just pass it around. It’s really very easygoing, everything. Because you know when you play music together almost every single day there’s no room for ego and for all that stuff because you know next time you’re going to be glad if you can pass something on to somebody else or you’re glad when somebody throws you something and it creates a very jovial, very respectful and very easy environment that way.
